correctness.rationale: The second coordinate is the preceding first coordinate, so the four cyclic recurrence equations are equivalent to return in the full plane. Every orbit has an assigned weak sign word; either assignment at a zero gives the same affine equation. The six necklaces exhaust the cases. Independent exact adjugate and determinant calculations in /workspace/review-checks/lozi4.py reproduce the three primitive lists and sign expansions and show nonsingularity also for constant and alternating words: the factors there are (a−b−1)(a+b+1)(a²+(b−1)²) and (a−b+1)(a+b−1)(a²+(b+1)²), respectively. Uniqueness and the rotational symmetry of those systems force lower period even with zero entries. The strict auxiliary signs and positive denominators make +++− always admissible, and ++−− and +−−− admissible just when P≥0. At equality rotating the latter to begin at its unique zero makes it a solution of the former system, hence the two are one orbit; the remaining sign pattern excludes smaller period. With t=a−b−1>0 the cubic P has strictly positive t derivative, and its t=0 sign comes from b²+2b−1. This yields the full boundary and the disappearance of an interior threshold at b=√2−1. The fourth-return determinants are b⁴ and traces ±a⁴+2b², with absolute trace greater than 1+b⁴ on the domain, giving smooth saddles where stated. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed.
